item.title: “Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating…
item.description:
“Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world. Ānanda, thus a monk is an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no descent of name-and-form. With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense-bases cease … such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.39

item.title: “The stream of craving flows everywhere, The creeper of craving sprouts and stands. Seeing that creeper that has arisen, Cut its root with wisdom.” “People,…
item.description:
“The stream of craving flows everywhere,
The creeper of craving sprouts and stands.
Seeing that creeper that has arisen,
Cut its root with wisdom.”

“People, immersed in sensual pleasures,
Delight in various pleasures.
Though they seek happiness,
They undergo birth and aging.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Bound by craving,
They undergo suffering for a long time.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Therefore, a monk who desires his own dispassion
Should abandon craving.”

From: Dhammapada 334-359

item.title: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a…
item.description:
“Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a dog, or a human were hung around their neck; so too, monks, that monk, examining the peril in those thoughts … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta

item.title: One with craving as companion Wanders for a long time — Now here, now there — He cannot stop The wandering of rebirth. Having understood…
item.description:
One with craving as companion
Wanders for a long time —
Now here, now there —
He cannot stop
The wandering of rebirth.
Having understood this danger —
That craving is the origin of suffering —
The monk, abandoning craving,
Not grasping, not clinging,
Mindfully dwells,
Living the homeless life.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Kulla: Kulla went to the charnel ground, Saw a woman abandoned, Thrown away in the cemetery, Food for worms. “Kulla, look at this body…
item.description:
Elder Kulla:

Kulla went to the charnel ground,
Saw a woman abandoned,
Thrown away in the cemetery,
Food for worms.

“Kulla, look at this body —
Diseased, foul, stinking,
Oozing, seeping,
Delighting fools.”

Having taken up the mirror of Dhamma,
I attained right view.
I contemplated this body —
Empty inside and out.

As it is below, so above,
As above, so below,
As below, so above,
As above, so below.

As by day, so by night,
As by night, so by day,
As before, so after,
As after, so before.

Such a one does not delight
In the five kinds of music.
When one-pointed,
Rightly meditating on the Dhamma.

From: Theragāthā 6.4
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner…
item.description:
“Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. Hatred, monks, is an inner stain … Delusion, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. These, monks, are the three inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries.”

From: Itivuttaka 88
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering;…
item.description:
“Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. This, monks, is called suffering. And what, monks, is the root of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there — that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.31
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick —…
item.description:
“Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and someone occasionally pours in oil and adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would burn for a long time. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are fetters — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises … Thus the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, just as an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick, and no one occasionally pours in oil or adjusts the wick — that oil lamp, being without its own fuel, with no further fuel added, not being nourished, would be extinguished. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing peril in things that are fetters — craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Thus the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.54
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them,…
item.description:
“Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them, then delight ceases. With the cessation of delight, lust ceases. With the cessation of lust, bondage ceases. Not being bound by the bondage of delight, Migajāla, that monk is called ‘one who dwells alone.’ Even if he lives in the midst of a village crowded with monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, royal ministers, ascetics of other sects and their disciples — still he is called ‘one who dwells alone.’ Why? Because craving, the companion, has been abandoned by him. Therefore he is called ‘one who dwells alone.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.63
📖 Read this sutta
